channel.title: Exotic Pet Care Hub — Field Notes
channel.description: Independent field guides to exotic pets.

item.title: Blue-Tongue Skink Obesity: Reading Fat Reserves in the Tail Before the Liver
item.description: A skink is meant to be broad across the back. It is not meant to be broad at the base of the tail, and that is where the fat that overwhelms the liver is stored.

item.title: Russian Tortoise Hibernation: The Weight Threshold That Decides Whether to Brumate
item.description: Brumation is not a calendar event, it is a metabolic budget. Below one ratio the animal has nothing to spend, and a fridge in November becomes the cause of death rather than the method.

item.title: Why Your Corn Snake Refuses Food in Winter — and When It Is Not Brumation
item.description: A four-month winter fast is normal biology. Losing a tenth of the body weight is not — here is how to tell them apart before you intervene.

item.title: Pacman Frog Setup: Why the Substrate Is a Chemical Filter, Not Decoration
item.description: An amphibian drinks through its skin, so the substrate is not decoration. It is the water supply, the filter and the infection risk in one layer.

item.title: Emperor Scorpion Molt Failure: The Humidity Window You Have About Six Hours to Hit
item.description: A scorpion has roughly six hours to finish moulting before its new shell hardens. Humidity is the only variable you actually control.

item.title: Hedgehog Torpor, Obesity and the Calcium-to-Phosphorus Ratio That Causes Both
item.description: Torpor, obesity and a lopsided calcium-to-phosphorus ratio are the same welfare problem caught at three different stages.

item.title: Gargoyle Gecko Handling: Reading Stress Before It Becomes a Tail Drop
item.description: A dropped tail never grows back. Here is what a gargoyle gecko tells you before it gets that far.

item.title: Leachianus Gecko Enclosure Size: Why the Minimum Is Bigger Than You Think
item.description: The largest gecko in the world does not fit in the smallest vivarium on the shelf. Here is the floor space it actually uses.

item.title: Axolotl Water Chemistry: The Nitrogen Cycle That Kills Them Quietly
item.description: Ammonia, then nitrite, then nitrate — the three numbers that decide whether an axolotl thrives or quietly burns.

item.title: Mexican Redknee Tarantula: Reading Pre-Moult Before She Seals Herself In
item.description: A tarantula that stops eating for six weeks is not starving. She is rebuilding an exoskeleton, and the humidity in those weeks decides whether she comes out of it intact.

item.title: Giant African Millipede Substrate: Depth, Calcium and the Chamber They Moult In
item.description: A millipede burrows, eats the soil and hardens its shell with calcium from it. A shallow, calcium-poor substrate is a slow starvation of the exoskeleton.

item.title: Chinchilla Dust Baths: Frequency, Humidity and the Skin Problems Overbathing Causes
item.description: Dust baths are coat care until the room passes 60 % humidity, at which point they start feeding a fungal problem instead of solving one.

item.title: Bearded Dragon Brumation: How to Tell a Normal Slowdown From a Sick Lizard
item.description: A bearded dragon that sleeps for ten weeks is following the season. One that sleeps at the wrong temperature is dying slowly, and from outside the glass the two look identical.

item.title: Sugar Glider Diet: The Calcium-to-Phosphorus Ratio Behind Hind-Limb Paralysis
item.description: Hind-limb paralysis in sugar gliders is usually nutritional, not neurological. The number that predicts it is a calcium-to-phosphorus ratio, and fruit does not supply it.

item.title: Panther Chameleon Hydration: Why Misting Twice a Day Still Leaves Them Dry
item.description: Chameleons do not drink standing water and they do not drink on demand. Hydration is a function of when the fog runs, not how wet the cage gets.

item.title: White's Tree Frog Oedema: Reading Fluid Retention Before the Lymph Hearts Fail
item.description: A frog that looks pleasingly plump is often a frog that is not moving fluid. The difference between a good body condition score and oedema is where the swelling sits.

item.title: Giant African Land Snail Shell Growth: Calcium, pH and the Rings That Record Both
item.description: A snail cannot repair a thin shell, only add to it. Every ridge on the whorl is a fortnight of whatever calcium the keeper happened to supply.

item.title: Degu Sugar Sensitivity: Why One Raisin Is a Different Risk Than One for a Rat
item.description: Degus are the only common pet rodent that cannot handle dietary sugar at all. The mechanism is a missing gene, and it makes fruit a species-inappropriate food rather than a treat.

item.title: Budgerigar Goitre: Why a Seed-Only Diet Swells the Throat
item.description: A budgie that squeaks instead of chirps and puffs at the throat is not fat and is not egg-bound. Its thyroid is enlarging against a trachea the width of a pencil lead.

item.title: African Grey Parrot Hypocalcaemia: The Seizure That Starts in the Seed Bowl
item.description: The first sign is usually a bird that falls off its perch. By then the ionised calcium has been sliding for months, and the seed mix is the reason.

item.title: How Often Should You Feed an Adult Jumping Spider?
item.description: A plump abdomen is a better calendar than any schedule. Here is what adult jumping spiders actually eat, how often, and the two feeding mistakes that shorten their lives.

item.title: The Best Bioactive Substrate Mix for a Crested Gecko Tank
item.description: Coir alone is not bioactive — it is a wet sponge. The mix that actually supports plants, springtails and a gecko that sheds cleanly, plus the drainage layer everyone skips.

item.title: How to Fix High Humidity and Mould in Isopod Cultures
item.description: Mould in an isopod tub is almost never a humidity problem. It is an airflow problem, and the fix takes five minutes and a drill.

item.title: Why Your Ball Python Is Refusing Frozen-Thawed Rats
item.description: Before you change the feeding schedule, change the thermometer. Nine out of ten feeding strikes are a temperature, security or presentation problem — in that order.

item.title: Do Leopard Geckos Need UVB — or Just a Heat Mat?
item.description: The honest answer is more interesting than either camp admits: leopard geckos are crepuscular, not nocturnal, and a low-level UVB zone changes how you supplement calcium.

item.title: Humidity and Salt Water Pools for Land Hermit Crabs
item.description: Hermit crabs do not drown in water — they drown in air that is too dry. The two-pool system, the substrate depth, and the gauge that decides whether they survive a moult.
